Hi Rita — thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap from our side:

- Primary objective: support FinEdge's real-time inference for document classification and named-entity extraction in production (customer-facing).
- Expected 95th p latency target: 120ms for single-request flows; bulk batch jobs can be higher.
- Estimated steady-state qps: 120 rps with 50% burst to 300 rps during peak windows.
- Data residency: US-only.

To move to a concrete Dedicated proposal we need a focused sizing session (60–75 minutes) to review exact traffic patterns, sequence lengths, and perf targets. Proposed agenda:
  1) Walk through the workload summary you shared (threads, payload sizes).
  2) Confirm latency SLOs and percentiles to optimize for.
  3) Map to model variants, batching, and caching options.
  4) Preliminary capacity recommendations and next steps (POC timeline).

Available slots (PDT):
- Tue 2026-06-16 09:00–10:15
- Wed 2026-06-17 13:30–14:45
- Thu 2026-06-18 11:00–12:15

If none of these work, drop a few windows that do. Also: could you attach a short sample of your payload distribution (avg tokens, 95th token lengths) and a week's qps histogram if you have it? That will make the call actionable.

I’m looping Marissa (solutions) and Dev (performance eng) — they’ll run the sizing on our side.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Preliminary answers to your asks:
- 95th p latency target: 120ms (hard requirement for UI flows).
- Typical payload: avg ~420 tokens, 95th ~2,100 tokens (we have a small number of long documents that hit that).
- Current production qps: steady 90 rps, spikes to ~280 rps during batch ingestion windows.

I've attached a brief workload summary (finedge_workload_summary.xlsx) and a quick dump of HPA metrics for last week (finedge_hpa_metrics.zip). We'll share a sanitized sample dataset if needed before the call.

One note: we may need to evaluate a mixed strategy — low-latency variants for UI and quantized larger models for bulk processing. Happy to discuss tradeoffs.

Thanks — see you Wednesday.
